entries.title: Model Citizen — stop gate + ownership journal for Claude Code / Codex
entries.why: Control plane under coding agents you already run: write rules/skills/roles/stances once as primitives; it projects them into Claude Code and Codex and enforces with hooks. Verified README features: graded shell-command hook (read-only→irreversible; autonomy stance decides which grades stop-and-ask), stop gate ("the turn doesn't end while your repo's own gate is red"), fresh-context review by agents that never saw the code, ownership journal so every file it touches is recorded and uninstall puts things back, per-session spend ledger exporting over OTLP (off by default). Mechanical form of three locks that are currently prose: code-decides-done as an enforced stop gate, install-agent-hooks.sh drift/revert via an ownership journal, and GYR reversibility tiers as a pre-execution grade. Explicitly not an LLM gateway or replacement runtime. MIT. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: Model Citizen: write agent rules once and enforce them with hooks
entries.whatItIs: A control layer under coding agents you already run: write rules, skills and roles once, and it applies them to two coding CLIs and enforces them with hooks. It grades shell commands by risk and keeps a turn open while the repo's own checks are red.
entries.whyItMatters: It would turn three of our written-only rules into machine checks: a real check decides done, install drift can be undone from a journal of touched files, and the green/yellow/red risk lanes grade commands before they run.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: a control-plane install, while code decides done and our reversibility lanes already gate done and risk (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: cachebeat — inactivity-triggered prompt-cache heartbeat (Claude Code)
entries.why: Tiny Claude Code skill: an inactivity-triggered silent heartbeat that keeps the prompt cache warm while a session sits idle, so the next message reads history from cache (~0.1× input) instead of re-billing the whole transcript. Fires only after true silence, re-arms itself, and self-kills after a deadline (default 8h) so an abandoned session cannot drip-bill. README math: "going cold once costs as much as ten heartbeats." Our seats are idle by design (Field Brief :32, 6h briefs, daily collect) and token-save is a locked priority — a long Fable/Opus EM session past cache TTL re-bills history on the next one-line check-in. Built-in deadline is already a kill condition shape. Claude-Code-only; Sept 2026 note: runs as a background shell task (beat.sh + SKILL.md) after monitors were capped at 30 min. $0, two files. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: cachebeat: keeps an idle session's prompt cache warm with a quiet ping
entries.whatItIs: A tiny skill for one coding CLI that sends a silent heartbeat while a session sits idle, so the next message reads history from cache instead of paying for the whole transcript again. It stops itself after a deadline so an abandoned session can't keep billing.
entries.whyItMatters: Our seats sit idle by design and saving tokens is a locked priority; a long coding session past the cache time limit pays again for its history on the next small check-in. Its readme says one cold start costs as much as ten heartbeats.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: it adds idle spend, and our Mac runs are one-shot jobs that exit (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: Gate Inbox — tmux board that surfaces sessions blocked on you
entries.why: Terminal board for running and triaging many AI coding-agent sessions in tmux: one list with live status so the session blocked on you is visible without hunting tabs. Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode run side by side each in its own tmux session; `i` walks everything waiting on you; agents started by hand appear as-is. README: "Gate Inbox reads the panes; it does not sit between you and the model." Our attention routing today is a markdown decision queue swept once at 09:09 PT — this is the live "who is blocked on Haiyuan right now" view that file is missing, adjacent to no-exit-while-waiting and the 540s watchdog. Read-only TUI over existing CLIs, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Small repo (Go). Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: Gate Inbox: a live board of agent sessions waiting on you
entries.whatItIs: A read-only terminal board that lists many coding-agent sessions with live status, so the one waiting on you is easy to spot. It reads each session's terminal pane and does not sit between you and the model.
entries.whyItMatters: Our decision queue is a file checked once at a set time; this would add a live view of who is blocked on Haiyuan right now. It sits next to our rule against exiting while waiting and the stall watchdog.

entries.title: crossagent — dual-agent tmux review with AGREE/ESCALATE/UNPARSED verdicts
entries.why: MCP server (npm crossagent-mcp) that pairs two coding agents in adjacent tmux panes — one drives, the other reviews. Every plan/diff passes through the peer; the reply always ends in a machine-parseable `VERDICT: <word>` with fixed vocabulary: AGREE / ADJUST / OBJECT / ESCALATE / UNPARSED. tmux is the only transport (no network, no shared file, no socket); briefing clears the peer's conversation so the reviewer is genuinely fresh. Gives blind dual-LGTM (Astra+Fable) an interface: today reviewers can return prose we adjudicate by reading; ESCALATE is "only the human can call it" (silent-misroute rule in mechanical form) and UNPARSED detects a non-verdict instead of treating it as assent (retry ceiling schema×1). Adopt the verdict contract as prose/checklist first; installing the MCP is optional/later. Requires Node 22+, tmux, Claude Code or Codex CLI. MIT. In playbook (2026-09-27, Haiyuan-approved) as the review verdict line (#review-verdict-line): VERDICT: APPROVE | REQUEST_CHANGES | ESCALATE @ head SHA; a missing line is UNPARSED and never an LGTM. MCP not installed.
entries.plainTitle: crossagent: one agent codes while a fresh peer reviews with a fixed verdict
entries.whatItIs: A tool server that pairs two coding agents in side-by-side terminal panes: one drives and the other reviews every plan and diff. Each review ends with a fixed, machine-readable verdict word, and the reviewer starts from a cleared conversation.
entries.whyItMatters: Now a playbook rule: each review ends with a verdict line (approve, request changes or escalate) for the PR's head commit, and a missing line never counts as approval. The tool server is not installed.
entries.statusNote: Adopted 2026-09-27 as the review verdict line: each review ends with one verdict on the head commit, and a missing line never counts as approval (#review-verdict-line).

entries.title: simply — ledger-owned done: judgment to models, gates to code
entries.why: tmux multi-agent harness where an auditor owns the work ledger + verification gates, a Claude Code PM owns the worker fleet, and completion travels a private file-based status ledger. Core rule: "Judgment to models; observation, loops, and gates to code" — agents cannot mark their own criteria passed; `verify` runs the checks and the settle gate stays open until every criterion passes and a QA package exists. Briefs state the outcome + observable criteria, not line-by-line steps ("the model owns the path; the ledger owns the destination"). Also ships max vs low-cost routing profiles (frontier for judgment, cheaper models for research/implementation), which mirrors our Opus-default / Kimi-fallback / flash-collect split. Import as prose + checklist for manage-handoffs and EM intent briefs (mechanical form of the rari promotion gate); no install, no new seat. In playbook (2026-09-25, Haiyuan-approved) as "code decides done": done = a deterministic check passed (tests / file / pushed commit / HTTP 200); self-reports and Jev completion_check are advisory only. Settle-gate/QA-package tooling not built.
entries.plainTitle: simply: models judge, code decides when work is done
entries.whatItIs: A multi-agent harness where an auditor owns the work ledger and the checks, and agents cannot mark their own criteria as passed. Work can't settle until every criterion passes and a QA package exists, and briefs give the outcome and criteria, not step-by-step orders.
entries.whyItMatters: We adopted its core rule: done means a real check passed, such as tests, a file, a pushed commit or a page that loads, and self-reports and decision-layer completion checks are advisory only. We have not built our own settle-gate or QA-package tooling.
entries.statusNote: Adopted 2026-09-25 as code decides done: only a deterministic check passing makes a task done; its settle-gate tools were not adopted (#code-decides-done; Maps/Decisions/2026-09-25-code-decides-done-and-replay-check.md).

entries.title: vnx-orchestration — per-dispatch NDJSON receipts + git worktree per worker
entries.why: Local control plane that drives installed coding CLIs (claude / codex / gemini / kimi / ollama) as subprocess workers, each in its own git worktree, through review gates, with an append-only NDJSON receipt per dispatch (verdict, provider, model, cost). No vendor SDK, so dispatches bill to existing CLI subscriptions (README reports measured cost=$0.0000 receipts). A receipt refuses to call a dispatch done without its PR, and branch protection is declared as YAML with a drift preflight. Patterns to adapt for the EM loop: a per-PR receipts.ndjson line per dispatch/review/merge (the grep-able "receipt complete" artifact for the promotion gate) and worktree-per-lane, so a dual-LGTM reviewer never touches the implementer's tree. Adopt the patterns, not the runtime. The author says it is not a security sandbox, and parallel worktree isolation is not yet race-free. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: vnx-orchestration: a receipt per agent job, each worker in its own copy
entries.whatItIs: A local controller that runs installed coding CLIs as workers, each in its own copy of the repo, through review gates. Every job adds a line to an append-only receipt log with verdict, model and cost, and a job isn't done without its PR.
entries.whyItMatters: Its patterns could fit our coding loop: one receipt line per job, review and merge, and a separate copy per lane so reviewers never touch the implementer's copy. The author says it is not a security sandbox, and isolation between parallel copies is not yet race-free.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: our kick ledger, receipt lines and done receipts already cover its per-dispatch receipts (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: agent-evals — record once, replay offline; gate on pass rate, cost p95, trajectory, calibrated judge
entries.why: Eval harness that records model calls once and replays them offline (no key, no network, runs in CI), then gates on pass rate, cost p95 (not mean), latency, and trajectory (catches right-answer-wrong-path, e.g. a refund that skips the lookup), with the LLM judge calibrated against human labels (agreement, Cohen's kappa, false passes, order/length bias). Shape for the rari promotion gate + Three-Run Proof trial: replay keeps repeat runs at $0, trajectory checks catch skipped steps, and any Jev/LLM gate promoted from shadow should report kappa + false passes, not a bare score. Caveat from its own README: the same suite scored 92% on replay but 28–44% live (mostly brittle exact-substring asserts), so replay is a regression guard, not proof of live quality. Small, new repo (created 09-23): borrow the pattern, don't add a dependency. In playbook (2026-09-25, Haiyuan-approved) as a light replay regression check inside Three-Run Proof, before skill/prompt promotion or Jev shadow→active; live Three-Run Proof stays the bar.
entries.plainTitle: agent-evals: record model calls once, then replay them offline as tests
entries.whatItIs: A test harness that records model calls once and replays them offline with no key or network, then gates on pass rate, high-percentile cost rather than the average, latency and the path the agent took. Its judge model is checked against human labels.
entries.whyItMatters: We added a light replay regression check inside the three-clean-runs rule, before promoting skills, prompts or a log-only decision-layer gate; live runs stay the bar. Its readme warns replay scored far higher than live, and we borrow the pattern, not the tool.
entries.statusNote: The replay check is a written promotion step, but its replay set is not built, so it cannot run; the tool was not adopted (#replay-check; #replay-set; Maps/Decisions/2026-09-25-code-decides-done-and-replay-check.md).

entries.title: rari (@0xwhrrari) — the Grok Bot operating system: handoff packet, reproduce-before-fix, stricter promotion gate
entries.why: Article (2026-09-03) that splits a Grok Bot setup into model + harness + loop + graph + approval layers, and argues for passing ownership, not transcripts. KEEP 1, structured handoff packet: every new Coding EM kick row and Manage → specialist handoff carries from / to / job_type / objective / artifacts / decisions / constraints / open_questions / next_gate. Manage passes it as the jev-shadow intake state, and Jev packet_complete is shadow only. KEEP 2, reproduce before fix: job_type=bug needs a repro artifact (steps, command, logs or failing test, env/versions) linked before the Opus 5.5 implementer launches; a failed repro parks the kick as blocked with the attempt recorded. KEEP 3, stricter promotion gate: Three-Run Proof stays at 3 runs (their 5-run minimum is skipped) plus rollback tested + receipt complete before moving up the ladder, and the Monday kill review adds weekly bot receipts, one Haiyuan spot-check of a real artifact, and 'would anyone miss this if removed?' → propose kill. Skipped because we already have them: CoS routing, reversibility approvals (GYR), autonomy ladder 0–4 with demotion (identical to ours), bounded retries, blind reviewers, shared-computer-is-not-isolation, and login handoff. In playbook §5/§12/§16 + checklist.
keeps: structured handoff packet (ledger + Manage handoffs; Jev intake shadow check)
reproduce-before-fix for job_type=bug (repro artifact before implementer; failed repro → blocked)
promotion gate = 3 clean runs + rollback tested + receipt complete; weekly receipts + one Haiyuan spot-check + 'would anyone miss this?'
entries.plainTitle: rari: structured handoffs, reproduce bugs first, and a stricter promotion gate
entries.whatItIs: An article that splits a chat-bot setup into model, harness, loop, graph and approval layers, and argues for handing over ownership, not transcripts.
entries.whyItMatters: We adopted three ideas: a structured handoff packet, a reproduction before the implementer starts on a bug, and a stricter promotion gate (three clean runs, a tested rollback, a complete receipt). The weekly kill review gains a Haiyuan spot-check.
entries.statusNote: Adopted 2026-09-25: the structured handoff packet, reproduce-before-fix on bug jobs and the stricter promotion gate with weekly receipts are standing rules (#handoff-packet; #promotion-gate).

entries.title: bounded-agent-runtime — run limits + tool risk tiers outside the LLM loop
entries.why: Hard ceilings enforced by the runtime, not the prompt (max_steps / max_seconds / max_usd / max_tool_calls / max_repeats loop detect), checked before each step and raised as exceptions; risk is a property of the tool (READ / WRITE / EXTERNAL / IRREVERSIBLE), not the agent's self-judgment. Shows how to move our 0xjmori run limits (50/2/$0/0) + GYR tiers from markdown into the grok-tmux-run / watchdog wrapper, with a hermetic model-free chaos test pattern. In playbook as a source pointer beside run limits + GYR (policy already live); runtime-enforced wrapper not built.
entries.plainTitle: bounded-agent-runtime: hard run limits enforced outside the model
entries.whatItIs: A runtime pattern where hard limits on steps, time, spend, tool calls and repeated loops are checked before each step, not left to the prompt. Risk belongs to each tool (read, write, external, irreversible), not to the agent's own judgment.
entries.whyItMatters: The playbook now cites it as a source beside our run limits and green/yellow/red risk lanes, which are already live as written policy. A wrapper that enforces them at run time has not been built.
entries.statusNote: The playbook cites it as a source for our written run limits and reversibility lanes, which are policy only; enforcing them outside the agent loop is not built (#run-limits).

entries.plainTitle: agent-runway: checks remaining quota before an agent job launches
entries.whatItIs: A command-line tool, skill and tool server that reads how much quota is used and when it resets across several coding CLIs, and answers proceed, defer or unknown.
entries.whyItMatters: It could run before each Field Brief launch and route straight to the fallback seat when quota is nearly used up, instead of waiting out a stall-watchdog timeout. A low-risk, green-lane smoke-test candidate only.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: no evidence that missed brief slots were quota, and it would change a collector script; still an uninstalled follow-up (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md; #usage).

entries.title: CAPO — quota-wall checkpoint + relaunch on the other CLI
entries.why: Detects Claude Code / Codex usage-limit cutoffs, writes a plain Markdown checkpoint of git status + uncommitted worktree changes, and relaunches the session on the other platform; when both are capped it parks until the earliest reset instead of flapping. Maps to our Opus → Kimi / Astra fallback and pairs with no-exit-while-waiting + the retry ceiling. Idea: a "quota limit checkpoint" exception branch in manage-handoffs / Mac launch skill. In playbook as a source pointer beside exception-first quota failover (Opus → Kimi live); auto checkpoint + relaunch not built.
entries.plainTitle: CAPO: save a checkpoint at a usage limit and resume on the other CLI
entries.whatItIs: A tool that notices when one of two coding CLIs hits its usage limit, saves a plain checkpoint of repo status and uncommitted changes, and relaunches the session on the other CLI. If both are capped, it waits for the earliest reset.
entries.whyItMatters: The playbook cites it as a source beside our quota failover, where a capped implementer already falls back to another seat. The automatic checkpoint and relaunch were not built.
entries.statusNote: The playbook cites it beside our live quota failover to a fallback seat; its automatic checkpoint and relaunch on the other tool were not built (#exception-first).

entries.title: ai-coding-gateway — PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook to trim noisy tool output
entries.why: Hooks Claude Code's PreToolUse / PostToolUse in ~/.claude/settings.json to strip ANSI colors, progress bars, passing-test lists, and build logs before the model reads them, plus global command allow/deny policy. Adapt the trimming hook pattern only (skip the GUI dashboard) to cut context bloat and premature compaction on long Fable/Opus test runs — a direct token-save lever. Lab card (adapted hook pattern); appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: ai-coding-gateway: trims noisy tool output before the model reads it
entries.whatItIs: Hooks that run before and after each tool call in one coding CLI and strip colors, progress bars, passing-test lists and build logs before the model reads them. It also adds an allow and deny list for commands.
entries.whyItMatters: Adapting just its trimming pattern could cut context bloat and early compaction of the chat history on our coding agents' long test runs, a direct way to save tokens. The card suggests skipping its dashboard.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: a global trim hook could hide test output reviewers need, and no bloat failure was measured (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: Company-in-a-Box — Jev research_check + completion_check (shadow)
entries.why: unicodef1wn X (2026-09-22): Jev as decision layer between manager and workers with four tools (route_worker, check_research, review_completion, guard_action). We already had route (intake) + guard (pre_tool); added research_check (Field Brief citation: accept|verify_more|reject) and completion_check (before done: complete|verify_more|incomplete) as SHADOW gates (honor:false, never block) plus intake live-worker-menu (available_workers/unavailable). Promote after Three-Run Proof.
entries.plainTitle: Company-in-a-Box: decision-layer checks for research and completion
entries.whatItIs: A social post describing a decision layer between a manager and its workers, with four tools: route work to a worker, check research, review completion and guard actions.
entries.whyItMatters: Our decision layer already had routing and guarding; we added a research check for Field Brief citations and a completion check before done, both shadow only and never blocking, plus a live worker list. Promotion waits for three clean runs.
entries.statusNote: Its research and completion checks run in our decision layer as shadow gates that log and never block, plus a live worker list; box-side, NOT VERIFIED that they still fire (#jev-gates).

entries.title: seanswarm multiagents-workflow — dual-read + fail-closed acceptance
entries.why: Skills-only pack (no new seat/runtime): dual-read of the same primary source with a match/addition/conflict table upgrades Field Brief source verification; fail-closed acceptance means prose "done" cannot pass without a mechanical artifact (test/exit-code/screenshot) or independent read-only diff-only review. Complements blind dual-LGTM (Astra+Fable) and CoS verification — does not replace either. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook true: folded into the playbook on 2026-09-23 (commit c72ebe6).
entries.plainTitle: multiagents-workflow: read sources twice; “done” needs proof or review
entries.whatItIs: A skills-only pack with no new seat or runtime. Its dual read has the same primary source read twice and tables what matches, adds or conflicts; its fail-closed acceptance rejects a prose “done” unless a test, exit code, screenshot or an independent read-only review of the diff backs it.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook: the dual read strengthens source checks for the Field Brief, and the pack adds to our two independent blind reviews and chief-of-staff verification rather than replacing either.
entries.statusNote: Adopted 2026-09-23: prose done cannot pass without a mechanical artifact or an independent read-only check, and brief skills prefer a dual read of key sources (Maps/Decisions/2026-09-23-lab-dsh-keeps-into-playbook.md).

entries.title: orchvia — code decides next step; park unknown outcomes
entries.why: Local Claude/Codex session engine with durable mailbox: "your code and the limits you configure decide what runs next, not a manager model." After a crash, work whose outcome is unknown waits for a human instead of auto-retry — the recovery half of our 0xjmori retry ceiling and the named 09-22 watchdog relaunch-vs-resume gap. Lab card / A/B experiment idea only; no install; appliedToPlaybook true: folded into the playbook on 2026-09-23 (commit c72ebe6).
entries.plainTitle: orchvia: code picks the next step, and unknown outcomes wait for a person
entries.whatItIs: A local session engine for two coding CLIs, with a durable mailbox, where “your code and the limits you configure decide what runs next, not a manager model.” After a crash, work with an unknown outcome waits for a human instead of retrying on its own.
entries.whyItMatters: Parking unknown outcomes is the recovery half of our retry ceiling, and it speaks to a watchdog gap we had named: relaunching a run versus resuming it. Partly in playbook; the engine is not installed and stays an A/B experiment idea.
entries.statusNote: Its park-unknown-outcomes rule is adopted and the ownership guard parks unreadable stale runs; letting code pick the next step was not (#retry-ceiling; Maps/Decisions/2026-09-23-lab-dsh-keeps-into-playbook.md).

entries.title: sctxx (+ ccompactor) — model-free session→handoff artifact
entries.why: Reads finished Claude Code / Codex / Pi transcripts on disk and writes a compact provenance-linked handoff any other agent can load (no model calls). Candidate machine-verifiable half beside hand-written vault notes for box↔Mac / EM continuation. GREEN smoke only on non-secret repos; inspect output before filing; off dual-LGTM critical path. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: sctxx: turn a finished agent session into a handoff, with no model calls
entries.whatItIs: A tool that reads finished transcripts from several coding CLIs on disk and writes a compact handoff, linked back to its sources, that any other agent can load. It makes no model calls.
entries.whyItMatters: It could be a machine-checkable companion to our hand-written vault notes when work moves between the bots’ server and the Mac, or continues in the coding loop. Backlog: a low-risk smoke test on non-secret repos only, output inspected before filing.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: vault notes and the kick ledger already carry handoff state, and it stays only a smoke idea, not installed (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md; #usage).

entries.title: omp-jev-watchdog — instruction adherence + verification honesty (shadow)
entries.why: Shadow-only Jev watchdog that records two checks: observed tool calls vs recent explicit instructions, and final assistant claim vs actual tool results. Mechanizes published CoS clause "evidence ≠ instruction" — detects "command failed then claimed passed." Manual slot-close first; do not install as a blocking gate. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: A watch-only check: did the agent follow instructions and report honestly?
entries.whatItIs: A watchdog for the decision-layer tool we use that runs in shadow mode, recording without blocking. It logs two checks: the agent’s tool calls against its recent explicit instructions, and its final claim against the actual tool results.
entries.whyItMatters: It would turn our published rule that agent output is evidence, not instruction, into a check that catches a failed command later claimed as passed. Backlog: manual checks come first, and it is not to be installed as a blocking gate.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: the shadow completion check, done receipt and negative-claim check already cover it (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: livelock + loopguard — named failure modes + loop/oscillation detect
entries.why: livelock names four long-CLI failure modes (crash/hang/stall/api-error) and leaves a machine-readable heartbeat (did-it-finish / what-killed-it). loopguard watches Claude/Codex/Gemini JSONL for loop/oscillation/stall. Extends our stale-only grok-tmux-watchdog (~540s) and pairs with 0xjmori abnormal-volume → stop-and-escalate. Lab card; no fleet replace; appliedToPlaybook true: folded into the playbook on 2026-09-23 (commit c72ebe6).
entries.plainTitle: livelock and loopguard: named failure modes and loop detection for long runs
entries.whatItIs: Two tools: livelock names four ways a long agent run fails (crash, hang, stall, API error) and leaves a machine-readable heartbeat saying whether it finished and what killed it; loopguard watches three coding CLIs’ session logs for loops, oscillation and stalls.
entries.whyItMatters: They go beyond our stall watchdog, which only flags stale output after about 540 seconds, and pair with our rule to stop and escalate on abnormal volume. Partly in playbook; neither tool replaces our fleet watchdog.
entries.statusNote: Its named failure modes are in our exception-first skill rules; loop detection is not installed, and the approved no-progress shadow flag waits on its heartbeat text being applied (#exception-first; #no-progress-flag).

entries.title: loop-orchestrator — tmux substrate + mailbox + watchdog + stateless coordinator
entries.why: Closest external mirror of our grok-tmux-run + stream-json + watchdog + EM heartbeat stack. Portable ideas: lane-readiness classifier + auto-restart watchdog as a named component; coordinator prompt assembled statelessly from files each tick; versioned additive-only substrate contract (CONTRACT.md). Lab card — appliedToPlaybook false (no same-day architecture gap).
entries.plainTitle: loop-orchestrator: terminal sessions, mailbox, watchdog and coordinator
entries.whatItIs: An open-source orchestrator for agent loops built on terminal sessions, with a mailbox, a watchdog, and a coordinator whose prompt is rebuilt from files on every tick instead of held in memory.
entries.whyItMatters: It is the closest outside mirror of our launch wrapper, streamed logs, stall watchdog and coding-loop heartbeat. Noted, with no architecture gap to fill that day; portable ideas include a lane-readiness check with auto-restart and a versioned, add-only contract.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: it mirrors our existing terminal, watchdog and heartbeat stack (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: bb-spec — mutually-blind agents + disk-docs-only handoffs
entries.why: Hardens blind dual-LGTM (Astra+Fable) + intent/spec/plan loop: implementer physically never sees the spec (only tests), so it cannot teach-to-intent; every stage hands off a file on disk, never chat memory. Complements (does not duplicate) 09-20 portable-llm-council SKIP. Lab card; no new seat.
entries.plainTitle: bb-spec: agents kept blind to each other, handing off only through files
entries.whatItIs: A workflow that keeps agents blind to each other: the implementer never sees the spec, only the tests, and every stage hands off a file on disk instead of relying on chat memory.
entries.whyItMatters: It could harden our two independent blind reviews and the intent, spec and plan steps of our coding loop. Noted only, with no new seat; it complements, and does not duplicate, a model-council tool we skipped.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: it conflicts with our rule that the implementer works from the committed plan (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: Intent-review stage — third oracle blind to PLAN.md
entries.why: Names EM failure mode: passed plan + passed tests but not what the user asked. Third review oracle checks final diff against verbatim original intent while blind to PLAN.md. Cheap process addition (intent → spec → plan → PR → dual LGTM); no new seat, no infra.
entries.plainTitle: Intent review: a third check of the final change against the original ask
entries.whatItIs: An extra review stage: a third reviewer checks the final diff against the user’s original request, quoted word for word, without seeing the plan. It targets work that passed its plan and tests but is not what the user asked.
entries.whyItMatters: This failure can happen in our coding loop of intent, spec, plan, PR and two blind reviews. Noted only: a cheap process step that needs no new seat or infrastructure.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: a third review seat costs tokens, and disproof criteria already come from the intent (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: Agent Chaperone — Jev MCP shadow-mode wrapper (backlog/smoke)
entries.why: Drop-in MCP wrapper (agent-chaperone -- <server>) to run TypeSafe Jev in shadow mode on Mac CLI MCP tools without changing servers or adding seats. Lab backlog/smoke only — not install-critical-path. Pair with Archestra 79% constant-trap calibration.
entries.plainTitle: Agent Chaperone: try decision checks in watch-only mode on agent tools
entries.whatItIs: A drop-in wrapper for tool servers that runs our decision layer in shadow mode, watching without enforcing, on the tools our Mac coding agents use.
entries.whyItMatters: It would let us test the decision layer on our agents’ tool calls without changing servers or adding seats. Smoke test only, not on the install path, to be paired with the Archestra calibration card.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: more decision-layer shadow volume with no gap to close (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: Foremerge — pre-merge intent/ChangeSet for parallel agents
entries.why: Local-first git-layer intent + ChangeSet declarations catch architectural collisions before merge when parallel Coding EM worktrees diverge on shared interfaces. Lab card; light vault handoff bullet (1-line target declaration) only — tool not installed.
entries.plainTitle: Foremerge: catch clashes between parallel agents before merging
entries.whatItIs: A local-first tool at the git layer where parallel agents declare their intent and change sets, so design clashes on shared interfaces surface before merge.
entries.whyItMatters: It targets a risk in our coding loop: parallel worktrees drifting apart on shared interfaces. Noted only: the tool is not installed, and the only takeaway is a light one-line target note in vault handoffs.
entries.statusNote: Only a one-line target declaration before parallel edits is in our handoff contract; the tool that catches clashes before merge is not installed (Maps/Contracts/manage-handoffs.md).

entries.title: Preflight — outbound secret-redaction proxy (backlog)
entries.why: Local reverse proxy that redacts credentials from outbound prompts/attachments before model dispatch. Lab backlog only — do not install. Pair with existing llmtap/cost-proxy backlog (dsh-llmtap-jev-guard-gbdl-2026-09-20).
entries.plainTitle: Preflight: strip secrets from prompts before they reach a model
entries.whatItIs: A local reverse proxy that redacts credentials from outgoing prompts and attachments before they are sent to a model.
entries.whyItMatters: It could keep keys out of what our agents send to models. Backlog only, not to be installed, and paired with the existing backlog idea of a cost-tracking proxy.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: a new proxy in the model path with no observed prompt-secret leak (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: Archestra — Jev 100-call calibration (79% constant trap)
entries.why: Field benchmark: naive ~75% accuracy can be worse than a benign constant (79% of calls are local status checks). Separate input authority vs output trust in Jev policy rubrics. Calibration KEEP for our Jev decision layer — no install. In playbook (2026-09-27, Haiyuan-approved) as the Jev constant baseline (#constant-baseline): a Jev gate must beat the always-majority constant before shadow→active.
entries.plainTitle: Archestra: why a decision check must beat always guessing the common case
entries.whatItIs: A field benchmark on agent calls: 79% were harmless local status checks, so a naive check at about 75% accuracy can do worse than calling every call harmless. A second lesson: keep input authority separate from output trust in policy rules.
entries.whyItMatters: Now a playbook rule, approved by Haiyuan: a decision-layer gate must beat a constant that always picks the majority answer before it moves from shadow to active. Kept as calibration only; nothing was installed.
entries.statusNote: Adopted 2026-09-27: a decision-layer gate must beat the constant majority answer before it goes active, which first narrowed one shadow gate (#constant-baseline).

entries.title: Portable DSH Multi-Agent Plugin (DSH seat watch/backlog)
entries.why: Scoped to existing DSH seat only: cross-provider review with host-enforced VERIFIED/UNCONVERGED verdicts. Lab watch/backlog — do not add as a new coding CLI seat; dual-LGTM remains Astra+Fable.
entries.plainTitle: A cross-provider review plugin for one of our existing coding seats
entries.whatItIs: A portable multi-agent plugin that runs reviews across model providers inside one existing coding seat, with the host enforcing a verdict of verified or not converged.
entries.whyItMatters: Watch list and backlog only: it stays scoped to that one seat, is not to be added as a new coding seat, and our two blind reviews keep their current two reviewer seats.
entries.statusNote: Set aside in the 09-27 triage: our two blind review seats stay as locked (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: Closed proof loop (Lingxi / Simon grok-bot-guide)
entries.why: Agents must return checkable proof (CI green, live URL, before/after screenshot) and push back until it matches — not soft done. Applied into manage-handoffs + Coding EM contract.
entries.source: x.ai Grok Bot for Engineering · Xiaohongshu grok-bot-guide-cn.pdf
entries.plainTitle: Closed proof loop: work counts as done only with checkable proof
entries.whatItIs: An idea from the bot platform’s engineering guide and a community guide: agents must return proof that can be checked, such as green CI, a live URL or a before-and-after screenshot, and work goes back until the proof matches.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook: written into the manager bot’s handoff contract and the coding loop’s contract, so a soft “done” is not enough.
entries.statusNote: A standing rule since 2026-09-20: soft done without checkable proof such as green tests, an exit code or a live page is pushed back (#spacex-keeps).

entries.title: Weekday specialist ops nudge (Jenny-style 1:1)
entries.why: 08:00 PT Mon–Fri Manage posts playbook bullets + blocker ask into Field Brief / Coding EM rooms so complex workflows do not drift.
entries.plainTitle: Weekday ops nudge: the manager bot posts reminders and asks for blockers
entries.whatItIs: A weekday routine from an engineer’s guide: at 08:00 PT, Monday to Friday, the manager bot posts playbook bullets and asks about blockers in the Field Brief and coding-loop rooms.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook as a standing weekday routine, styled on a one-to-one check-in, so complex workflows do not drift.
entries.statusNote: Merged into the Monday card sync and its weekday routine later deleted, so no weekday nudge runs; the Monday part is NOT VERIFIED (Maps/Decisions/2026-10-05-hub-factual-drift-published.md; #changelog-2026-10-19).

entries.title: PR board sweep every 12h
entries.why: 09:00 + 21:00 PT daily: scan open PRs (CI/conflicts/stall) → Coding EM Mac CLI unblock + proof. Retargeted from 30m to 12h per Haiyuan.
entries.plainTitle: PR board sweep: scan open PRs every 12 hours for anything stuck
entries.whatItIs: A routine from an engineer’s guide: at 09:00 and 21:00 PT, scan open PRs for CI problems, merge conflicts or stalls, and send them to a Mac coding agent to unblock, with proof.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook as a standing routine. Haiyuan moved it from every 30 minutes to every 12 hours.
entries.statusNote: A standing routine: the PR board sweep runs at 09:09 and 21:09 PT for failing checks, conflicts and stalls, and it never merges (#spacex-keeps).

entries.title: Nightly Mac harness audit (03:00 PT)
entries.why: Overnight rotate one Mac CLI for scoped audit PR on BQAA (or named repo); dual-LGTM; no merge. Morning ping only if ready or blocked.
entries.plainTitle: Nightly Mac harness audit: one coding agent opens a scoped audit PR
entries.whatItIs: An overnight routine at 03:00 PT: one Mac coding agent, chosen in rotation, opens a scoped audit PR on a set repo or another named one, and the PR gets two blind reviews.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook as a nightly routine. It does not merge, and it sends a morning ping only if the audit is ready or blocked.
entries.statusNote: A standing routine at 02:59 PT: one rotating Mac seat opens a scoped audit PR for blind review, with a morning ping if it is ready (#spacex-keeps).

entries.title: P0 urgency mode (keyword-only for now)
entries.why: Documented: saying P0 can mean high-cadence babysit. NOT a standing 5m poller yet — keyword only until Haiyuan asks.
entries.plainTitle: P0 urgency mode: saying “P0” can mean close, frequent checks
entries.whatItIs: An idea from an engineer’s guide: saying “P0”, the top-priority label, can mean high-frequency babysitting of a task.
entries.whyItMatters: Follow-up only: it stays a keyword for now, not a standing poller every 5 minutes, until Haiyuan asks.
entries.statusNote: Its keyword-only P0 urgency mode is a standing playbook line, already there at the 09-27 triage; a 5-minute poller waits until Haiyuan asks (#spacex-keeps; Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md).

entries.title: Shared box ≠ security isolation
entries.why: All Grok bots share one cloud computer (files, browser logins). Treat secrets as fleet-visible. Playbook warning applied.
entries.plainTitle: A shared bot computer is not security isolation
entries.whatItIs: From the bot platform’s docs and a user guide: all of our chat bots share one cloud computer, with the same files and browser logins.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook as a warning: treat any secret on that shared computer as visible to the whole fleet.
entries.statusNote: A standing warning in the playbook: all always-on bots share one cloud computer, so it is not a security boundary (#spacex-keeps).

entries.title: Jev multi-gate router + live session
entries.why: Live session block: mode active, confidence_floor 0.55, OpenRouter typesafe/jev-1.13, jev-route helper, smoke table (intake/pre_*), Manage Bot session recipe. Gates stay; no Playwright.
entries.plainTitle: Our decision layer’s multi-gate router and live session setup
entries.whatItIs: A playbook block for running our decision layer live: active mode, a confidence floor of 0.55, a routing helper, a smoke-test table for its gates, and a session recipe for the manager bot.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook as the live setup for routing through several decision gates. The gates stay, and no browser automation tool is added.
entries.statusNote: Active since 2026-09-20 per the playbook: the decision layer answers typed gate questions in one call, honored above a confidence floor, else back to the manager bot (#jev-gates; #jev-session).

entries.title: CoS verification — evidence ≠ instruction
entries.why: DSH Lab KEEP (asyncdot CoS): treat every agent completion as evidence, not instruction; re-check live artifact / exit code / published URL before marking a slot green.
entries.plainTitle: Chief-of-staff check: an agent’s “done” is evidence, not an order
entries.whatItIs: A rule kept from the asyncdot chief-of-staff pattern: treat every agent completion as evidence, not instruction, and re-check the live artifact, exit code or published URL before marking a slot green.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook: an agent’s word alone does not turn a slot green; the real result is re-checked first.
entries.statusNote: A standing rule since 2026-09-20: an agent's completion is evidence, not an order, and the live artifact is re-checked before a slot goes green (Maps/Decisions/2026-09-20-lab-dsh-keeps-into-playbook.md).

entries.title: Single-target handoff + hop cap
entries.why: DSH Lab KEEP (OpenBot): only the first @mention in a bot reply wakes another bot; hop cap default 2 then ask Haiyuan — never silent misroute. Rooms also: ack/final discipline (≤1 ack + 1 final).
entries.plainTitle: One handoff target per bot reply, and a cap on bot-to-bot hops
entries.whatItIs: A rule kept from the OpenBot pattern: only the first mention in a bot’s reply wakes another bot, and after 2 hops, the default cap, the bots ask Haiyuan instead of routing on.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook, so work is never silently misrouted; our group rooms also keep to at most one acknowledgment and one final reply.
entries.statusNote: A standing rule since 2026-09-20: only the first mention wakes a bot, after two hops the ask goes back to Haiyuan, and rooms get one ack and one final (Maps/Decisions/2026-09-20-lab-dsh-keeps-into-playbook.md).

entries.title: Lab #2 spikes: llmtap / jev-guard / GBDL (backlog)
entries.why: DSH 2026-09-20 backlog only — not installed: llmtap per-seat cost proxy; jev-guard Coding EM smoke; GBDL-shaped vault export of bot defs (convention). Playbook notes under §11 Lab follow-ups.
entries.plainTitle: Three parked spikes: per-seat cost, a guard smoke test, bot exports
entries.whatItIs: Three backlog ideas from one Lab scouting round: llmtap, a proxy that tracks cost per coding seat; a smoke test of a decision-layer guard in the coding loop; and a vault export of bot definitions in a set format, as a convention.
entries.whyItMatters: They point at per-seat spend tracking and keeping bot setups on file. Backlog only and not installed; the playbook lists them under Lab follow-ups.
entries.statusNote: The 09-27 triage kept all three spikes parked, and Haiyuan retired jev-guard for good on 2026-10-25 (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md; Maps/Decisions/2026-10-25-jev-guard-retired.md).

entries.title: jev-browser Lab backlog (no Playwright)
entries.why: KEEP candidate parked: Playwright + Jev click decisions. Do not install Playwright. pre_browser gate already filters computerUse.
entries.plainTitle: Parked idea: browser clicks decided by our decision layer
entries.whatItIs: A parked candidate: pair a browser automation tool with our decision layer so the layer makes the click decisions.
entries.whyItMatters: Backlog only: the browser tool is not to be installed, and an existing gate before browser actions already filters computer-use requests.
entries.statusNote: Kept as parked backlog: no browser automation is installed, and the existing pre-browser gate covers the decision (Hunt/agent-manage/2026-09-27-lab-to-playbook-triage.md; #usage).

entries.title: Harness engineering: Codex in an agent-first world (OpenAI)
entries.why: Repo/docs as system of record: short indexes, durable specs/plans, decision logs, linted invariants, doc-gardening. Maps onto our EM intent/spec/plan + dual-LGTM and vault Decisions.
entries.plainTitle: Harness engineering: the repo and its docs as the system of record
entries.whatItIs: A model maker’s engineering post on agent-first work: keep the repo and docs as the system of record, with short indexes, lasting specs and plans, decision logs, invariants checked by linters, and regular doc cleanup.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook: these ideas map onto our coding loop of intent, spec and plan with two blind reviews, and onto the decision notes in our vault.
entries.statusNote: Applied 2026-09-16: coding work runs from committed intent, spec and plan files with decision logs, and doc upkeep is part of the daily consolidation (#em-loop; Maps/Decisions/2026-09-16-lab-scout1-applied.md).

entries.title: How we built our multi-agent research system (Anthropic)
entries.why: Lead plans → fan-out collectors → persist artifacts → synthesize + citation-check. Direct template for Field Brief collect→brief→publish and Manage CoS effort budgets.
entries.plainTitle: “How we built our multi-agent research system”: lead agent plus collectors

entries.title: Uncle Bob agent code-quality loop — short instructions, small steps, automated gates, then mutation and CRAP hardening and Gherkin acceptance
entries.why: Code-quality loop for coding agents in five stages, as summarized from an image Haiyuan shared on 2026-10-10: short instructions, small steps, automated gates, hardening with mutation testing and CRAP scores, and acceptance written in Gherkin (Given / When / Then). No URL: that image is the only source and its author is not identified, so href is this Lab page, not a source, and the Uncle Bob name is how the loop was shared, not checked here. CRAP (change risk) is comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp per function, where comp is its cyclomatic complexity and cov its test coverage from 0 to 1; over 30 is the usual cut-off, and a function whose complexity is over 30 scores over 30 at any coverage, so it needs splitting, not more tests. Already applied, per the harness playbook: dual review → human merge. Also applied: #522, report-only mutmut on the BQAA SDK, schedule or manual only and never a merge gate: 972 mutants, 70.9% score, 272 survivors (kick-ledger numbers; (972 − 272) / 972 would be 72.0%, so check #522's report before quoting a killed count), the survivors now a nightly-audit follow-up. Not yet: CRAP scoring and Gherkin acceptance. Design notes drafted 2026-10-11 (nothing run): report-only CRAP next to #522 (coverage.py plus radon or lizard, schedule or manual, never a gate, its top functions fed to the nightly audit as test-writing themes), and Coding EM kick done-when written as Given / When / Then, each Then a check code can run, or tagged for review when it needs judgment. Fit: code decides done, the closed proof loop, disproof review (reviewers take their rejection criteria from the done-when), and the mutation-testing Lab cards (Kanon's a guard must be able to fail, corralai's planted faults). Caveats: CRAP rewards coverage, not assertions, so a test that runs a line without checking it lowers CRAP while that line's mutants survive, so CRAP sits next to mutation, not in place of it; per-function coverage from line spans is approximate, and radon and lizard count complexity differently, so one tool is picked and pinned; Gherkin here covers the kick contract, not executable acceptance tests inside the SDK, which would need step definitions and a runner. Any workflow, kick-template or playbook change needs Haiyuan. No new seat. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: ScaleMAS: bounded sharing during collection
entries.why: ScaleMAS (Qi et al.) has identical, role-free agents work asynchronously through one append-only store per task: they publish results with references to what they built on, search it with BM25 plus a decaying citation weight (at most 8 messages per call), and visit messages by address. With a 9B model the authors report BrowseComp-Plus accuracy rising from 38.1% with one agent to 65.3% with 16; on SWE-bench Verified, 4 agents matching the 80.0% of 8 independent agents with about half the tokens (15.3M against 28.3M per example); and, at 8 agents, BrowseComp-Plus falling from 60.0% to 40.8% when the citation weight is removed. Proposed experiment (playbook §6, Field Brief pipeline): with the three existing collector seats and equal total token budgets, compare the current pack workflow (one pack per seat, all read for the brief) against task-local sharing of intermediate results with bounded BM25 retrieval, then add citation weighting as a separate ablation. Measure verified coverage and false claims in the selected final brief, duplicate tool calls, total tokens and elapsed time; the runs include a misleading but popular finding and a collector dropout. Adopt only if verified output improves or equal quality costs less; stop if citation ranking amplifies false findings. Promotion only via §16's existing gate (three clean runs, rollback tested, receipt complete); reviewer findings stay out of the shared pool so review stays blind. Caveats: the three third-party benchmarks run on 100 items each (the first 100, or all of FATE-H) with no variance or error bars reported for the headline numbers, and are scored Pass@N: the group counts as right if any of its N agents is right (so part of the 1-to-16 rise is extra tries), and choosing the final answer is called orthogonal and never tested, which is why the experiment scores the selected brief. ScaleMAS's large relative gains over debate and shared-context baselines are on Contradiction Audit, the authors' own LLM-built benchmark, where a contradiction counts as found if any reported pair includes its edited snippet and false reports cost nothing: debate and shared-context baselines never exceed 7% there in the 9B runs, while ScaleMAS reaches 29.4% at 16 agents and 50.9% at 128. Citation-quality evidence is partly circular: among examples whose correct answer cites a message, 85% of the most-cited fifth of messages lie on a correct answer's evidence chain against 29% of the least-cited, but that chain is traced through citations, as the authors acknowledge; messages naming gold evidence do draw about twice the citations of those naming other sources. Self-citations and replies that correct or contradict a message also add to its weight, so popularity cannot stand in for verification. The cap bounds each call, not total context or cost: an agent's intake grows with how often it reads, and on FATE-M at 8 agents BM25-only ranking read twice the tokens of the default (5.7M against 2.7M) under the same cap. The store is discarded after each task, so it is no evidence against our durable memory loop. The paper's role-free agents run with no human gate or reviewer, so the results do not justify replacing our lanes, human gates or blind review. Nothing has been run; any workflow change needs Haiyuan. No new seat. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: Deeper, not bigger: a depth check for briefs
entries.why: Felix Rieseberg's post "How to be more ambitious: A tutorial for humans with models" (2026-10-13) names four types of ambition: speed (the same work in less time), altitude (going up in abstraction to the outcome rather than the individual task), depth (considering a task the way a field-leading expert would, going one level deeper to the underlying data, tools and problems) and range (drawing on multiple fields rather than just the one the task might need at the surface). For depth it gives a prompt asking for "a deeper version of this task, not a bigger one": before rewriting the prompt, the model says what a top professional in the field would do that was not asked for, names the rawest material they would start from instead of what has already been digested, names the specific methods and tools they would use, and says what, other than the model or the user, would show the result is right. Adopted: an optional depth-check step in research and draft briefs (vault templates/research-draft-brief.md; Decision Maps/Decisions/2026-10-15-depth-check-brief-step.md) with four prompts: what a top professional would do that the brief does not ask for; the rawest sources rather than summaries; that professional's specific methods and tools; and what outside check shows the result is right, which points to our existing blind review and done receipts rather than adding a new check. Already had: an outside judge (the post: do not ask the model to judge itself) in blind Astra/Fable review instead of self-grading, and in our code-decides-done checks where a tool can verify; outcome-level goals (the post's altitude) in routines such as the PR board sweep and the stuck-job check (the Coding EM kick pickup check); and specialist bot lanes, though they are only a partial match for the post's range, which means bringing several fields into one task. Nothing has been measured yet, and the post reports no results for the prompt either, only that it often helps the author. Not in the playbook: the step lives in the vault template and the Decision note. No new seat. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: lastlight-pr-gate: push gate needing a fresh-session review at the exact SHA
entries.why: Pre-tool-use hook plugin for a coding-agent CLI whose rule is that no unreviewed commit reaches a remote: a push needs a review recorded locally at that exact SHA, run with the review assets of the PR-review service the plugin is named for. The review must come from the plugin's run script, which runs it in a fresh headless session that did not write the code and writes attestation.json binding the result to the head SHA and a hash of the exact diff read; the recorder refuses a marker without a matching attestation, so a hand-written findings.json is rejected. The reviewed diff is untrusted input: the review runs in a disposable git clone under the OS sandbox, with credential stores denied and egress limited to the API, and only findings.json is copied back out. Containment is verified, not assumed: because a settings file that fails validation is silently ignored in headless mode, the runner first attempts a real escape and refuses to go on if the canary survives. A pre-commit review of the working tree is advisory and cannot satisfy the gate, since its attestation carries an empty SHA, which the recorder refuses by design. The pass bar is no findings, or every finding dismissed with a stated reason of at least 25 characters. The gate covers git push in its various spellings, the PR create, ready and reopen commands and API POSTs to a pulls endpoint, and it denies the code host's MCP write tools outright; reads and merges are never gated, and the check needs no network and fails closed. It also ships a work sandbox built on a clone, not a worktree, because a worktree's git dir lives inside the real repository; its README's two-layer table says the filesystem sandbox confines the processes the shell tool spawns but not the file-writing tools, permission rules cover file edits but not spawned processes, and neither confines the environment, so the review session starts from an empty environment (env -i) with a keep-list. The author states the limit plainly: it is not tamper-proof; it makes the honest path easy and stops a stale review vouching for new code. Why it matters here: every blind review of ours ends with exactly one machine-readable verdict line on the head SHA; a review with no parseable line, or one naming an older SHA, is UNPARSED and never counts as an LGTM, and dual LGTM means two APPROVE lines on the current head SHA (#review-verdict-line). The collection pack calls that rule prose discipline today; the attestation is the same rule as a check that can fail, bound to a hash of the diff the reviewer read, so a review recorded at one SHA cannot vouch for new code and hand-written findings are refused. We already have: blind dual review in which the implementer is never a reviewer on the same PR (#em-loop), which the pack notes is roster discipline, not enforced by construction; anything an agent reads, PR text and tool output included, treated as data, never instructions (#untrusted-content); and the rule that a new check is first run against a deliberately broken input and seen to fail (#check-can-fail), which the escape probe applies to a sandbox. What would be adopted, per the collection pack's recommendation (a proposal, not approved): the attestation format and gate contract as playbook prose first, that is, a marker bound to head SHA, diff hash, reviewer model and sandbox posture, written only by a fresh session that did not write the code, with hand-written findings refused; reviewed diffs handled in a disposable clone with only findings copied back, after an escape probe proves containment, so that a silently ignored setting fails closed; advisory pre-commit review kept structurally unable to satisfy the gate; dismissals with a stated reason; and reads and merges never gated. A live push gate would change every seat's ship path, so it is a separate Haiyuan decision. Caveats: it is tied to the service's packaged review assets, so only the attestation and gate pattern would carry over, not the service dependency; its hooks fit one coding-agent CLI, and sandbox behaviour differs by platform, so containment would have to be probed per seat; the test counts in its README (245, 16, 133, 119 and 142 cases across five suites, as printed by the suites) are the author's and were read, not re-run; MIT, 0 stars, created 2026-09-04; README-verified only, not installed or run. Reference only; any workflow change, live-seat install, hook or settings change needs Haiyuan. No new seat. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: Driftproof: with/without-skill evals that issue model-bound receipts
entries.why: Open-source tool that measures whether a SKILL.md still helps after the model underneath changes: it runs the skill's own eval tasks with and without the skill, judges each answer several times and issues a receipt bound to the model version saying the skill clearly helps, clearly hurts, makes no clear difference, or had too few answers to tell. Its credibility rule is to report bands (mean ± standard deviation) and to claim a change only when the bands do not overlap and the difference clears a 0.05 effect floor, never on either alone; in the author's words, "a tool that cries wolf is worse than no tool". Since receipt spec v0.5 it samples the generation as well as the judge, 3 to 10 draws per arm, each judged repeatedly, with a stopping_reason recorded; the author's Report #006 found draw-to-draw standard deviation of up to 0.186, larger than the judge's noise. It consumes an existing eval format for skills, and a run refuses up front if the projected calls or dollars exceed its caps (DEV_MAX_CALLS, DEV_MAX_USD). Reference data from the author's Report #005 (30 cells): a skill's cost when it fires is driven mainly by the input it makes the model pull in rather than by its own length (input delta against cost r = +0.92, the skill's own length r = +0.33), and one 738-token skill drew 34 times its own size in extra input. Why it matters here: the collection pack notes that our skills are mirrored across six seats on one-time verdicts that nobody re-checks when the model underneath changes, while verdicts age because the substrate moves. A dated receipt bound to the model version answers the recalibrate-or-retire question (does each rule still earn its place when a model changes?) with evidence instead of memory, and the pack places it next to Harness Wrangler's card (paired harness experiments, ablation, trigger sets) on an axis Wrangler does not price: model-bound skill receipts over time and the marginal cost of firing. We already have: before a skill or prompt change is promoted, a few saved runs are replayed to confirm nothing regressed, and a replay pass means nothing broke, not that the change is good (#replay-check); three runs can catch a large regression, but three clean runs do not show that a smaller one is absent (#detection-floor); and long runs inherit $0 spend without Haiyuan's approval (#run-limits). What would be adopted, per the collection pack's recommendation (a proposal, not approved), as promotion-gate prose with one pilot skill named: each shared skill carries 3 to 5 human-approved eval cases grounded in claims its SKILL.md makes; a with/without run issues a dated receipt naming the model version; the decision rule is band non-overlap plus the 0.05 floor, with generation sampled, so a single judged answer never decides; runs refuse before spending past call and dollar caps, and the same receipt prices the marginal cost of firing (the input pulled in, not the skill's length); and a model change in any seat re-queues receipts for the skills that seat loads. Caveats: this card is the pattern plus the author's reference data; any metered run is spend and needs Haiyuan, who also chooses between a subscription and a metered API path, and standing scheduled runs would be recurring spend; judge noise is real, and bands reduce it without removing it, so the author advises re-running a surprising verdict before acting on it; eval cases need approval skill by skill; every report number is the author's run, not ours; Apache-2.0, 2 stars, created 2026-07-28; README-verified only, not installed or run. Reference only; any workflow change, live-seat install, hook or settings change needs Haiyuan. No new seat. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: keel: verifiers try to refute serious findings; review depth is priced
entries.why: Workflow plugin for a coding-agent CLI that plans, builds and independently verifies a change, with the verification depth priced per change, verification only: gates only about $0.2, Basic about $0.25 to 0.5, Standard about $1.4 to 4.3 and Maximum about $2.7 to 7.6. Its doctrine is that a false alarm is a cost, not a bonus: serious findings go to separate verifiers that try to refute them, a finding QA "proved" that keel cannot reproduce becomes "unclear", and anything not checked is labelled "not verified". The author's measurements (a blind-scored set of 8 changes with 17 known defects, keel 1.0, October 2026): one plain reviewer, about $0.22, found 15.5 with 4 false alarms in 8 runs; Basic, about $0.34, found 15.3 with 0 false alarms in 24 runs; Standard, about $2.4, found 16.3; Maximum, about $5, found 17 with 0 false alarms in 8 runs. Counting only must- and should-fix items, Basic and Standard each found 15 of 17 and Maximum 14. The author says plainly that keel does not make review cheaper, it makes it cleaner, and that on this set Basic's fix list matched Standard's on every change. Hard steps (confirmations, the verification record before a finish, and keel's own git step: no secret files, no AI attribution, no commit on main) are hooks and scripts, not prompts; every end of work shows tokens, dollars and plan share per agent; and tasks (a branch and folder each) and sessions (a handoff note) are separate lanes that never mix in one conversation. Why it matters here: the collection pack calls it the first priced false-alarm measurement for our disproof-review lane, and notes that our reviews state rejection criteria up front but never cost a false alarm or report not verified as a first-class label inside the fix list, nor count a false alarm's cost inside our one-fix-round budget (now three fix rounds, then escalate: Haiyuan 2026-10-20 02:39 PT). We already have: blind reviewers who ask what would make a change unacceptable, name 2–3 rejection criteria from the task contract before reading the diff, return evidence on FAIL and list what was tried on PASS (#disproof-review); final done reports with a NOT VERIFIED section, what was not checked, never omitted (#done-receipt); public PR review comments from our review seats that carry only P0s, P1s and merge-blocking P2s (#review-posts-blockers); and the always-on play of skills for advisory policy and hooks for must-hold rules (#em-loop), which keel follows for its hard steps. What would be adopted, per the collection pack's recommendation (a proposal, not approved), as review-contract prose with no install: a refutation pass by a separate verifier before findings become must- or should-fix, with unreproduced "proofs" downgraded to unclear and unchecked areas labelled not verified finding by finding; depth chosen by price, with the price shown before and after (gates only, basic, deep), defaulting to shallow unless the change touches money, access, migrations or widely depended-on code; per-agent token and dollar rows in end-of-work reports; and hard steps (the verification record before finish, git hygiene) kept in hooks and scripts, not prompts. Caveats: the numbers are the author's single test set (8 changes, 17 defects; Maximum one run per change), directionally useful but not our fleet's rates; it runs in one coding-agent CLI only today; MIT, 0 stars, created 2026-10-15; README-verified only, not installed or run. entries.title: rollcage-guard: one secret-guard rules file for four coding-agent tools
entries.why: Single local binary (a signed, notarized build that runs locally and sends nothing) that installs one rules file as a pre-tool-use guard in four coding-agent tools, through each tool's own hook. It blocks reads of secret files (.env files, ~/.ssh, a cloud provider's credentials folder, *.pem and *.key files, infrastructure state files, service-account JSON; .env.example is allowed), environment dumps (printenv, /proc/*/environ, keychain reads), inline interpreter one-liners that read environment variables, and destructive commands; it asks before risky, cloud and production commands and before pushes to protected branches; before a git commit or git push it scans the staged changes and outgoing commits for keys; and it blocks exfiltration domains. Where a tool's hook cannot ask, ask becomes a block. explain "COMMAND" previews a verdict, and status and log show coverage and recent blocks, with keys masked in the log. The README states its limits: it fails open on an internal error, it is a guardrail, not a sandbox, it matches patterns, and it covers only agents that have hooks. The same rules are also offered as an advisory public MCP server, which advises while the hook enforces. Why it matters here: per the collection pack, our kept guards are single-seat (cheat-drill probes one coding-agent CLI's hooks; tamperproof and bouncer are shaped for that CLI) while the fleet runs six seats, and this is one deterministic rules file for several CLIs, with a key scan at commit and push, the moment a key actually leaves, and an explain preview so a rule can be tested before it fires. We already have: a forbidden.md ban on secret disclosure, which the pack notes is enforced only as per-seat prose, and the always-on play that keeps skills for advisory policy and hooks for must-hold rules, no secrets in the diff among them (#em-loop). What would be adopted, per the collection pack's recommendation (a proposal, not approved): a reversible trial of one shared rules file on the two of our seats whose CLIs it supports, warn and log first, then block, with uninstall as the rollback; the staged and outgoing-commit key scan at commit and push; an explain-style preview and a masked block log, plus a cheat-drill pass before trusting any coverage number; and the guard kept local-only, without the public MCP endpoint. Fleet-wide standing enforcement would change shared seat config, a separate Haiyuan decision. Caveats: it fails open by design, so a guard bug allows the call and the log has to be watched; it matches patterns and is not a sandbox; a third tool it supports may match the hook surface of one more of our seats, but that fit was not verified, so no coverage of that seat is claimed; the advisory MCP endpoint was not fetched or graded; it is the open-source core of a commercial desktop app, and only the core would be tried; MIT, 1 star, created 2026-10-14; README-verified only, not installed or run. Reference only; any workflow change, live-seat install, hook or settings change needs Haiyuan. No new seat. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: pair-mailbox: one writer, sealed-patch critic, turns end on a mailbox read
entries.why: Two-agent pair protocol for independent coding-agent CLIs (Python 3 standard library only; tmux and git required; profiles for six CLIs). Exactly one agent holds write authority, and its MCP server enforces the single-writer rule at the protocol level, logging refusals to an append-only audit transcript; the critic works read-only and proposes changes only as SHA-256-sealed patch files (mode 0600) whose hash the writer verifies immediately before applying them, a hash seal, not a signature, as the author says. Its core delivery rule is "The Mailbox Is the Guarantee, Delivery Is the Accelerator": a turn ends with a bounded pair_read(wait_seconds=N), so an agent is never idle with unread mail, while pair_deliver, which types a pointer into the peer's tmux pane, is best-effort only, since a full-screen TUI hides it. Mailbox files are atomic and numbered monotonically under flock, and the peer or a watchdog confirms allowlisted [y/N] prompts. An autonomy setting decides how far the pair runs alone: the default, auto, works a round through to a finished PR with no human word; semi needs recorded evidence and one human ok at verify; secrets, deploys, migrations, deletions and git history stop the pair at every level. Its own table names a weakness: pair_evidence is agent-reported and the close gate trusts it, so rounds refuse to close without it, but it is self-declared. Why it matters here: it is the enforced version of our written-handoff discipline for two live seats. A server-refused single writer plus sealed-patch review is implementer ≠ reviewer with a code boundary, and ending each turn with a bounded read makes the mailbox a guarantee rather than a hope, preventing the stall where an agent sits idle with unread mail in headless tmux work. We already have: every handoff from Manage to a specialist carries a machine-readable packet (#handoff-packet), and the pack notes that Manage handoffs already assume this discipline in prose; the implementer is never a reviewer on the same PR (#em-loop); done means a concrete, deterministic check passed, such as tests green, the expected file present, a commit pushed or a live URL at HTTP 200, and self-reports are advisory only (#code-decides-done); merges, payments, unsolicited publishes and agent deletion require Haiyuan (#thesis); and agent-perch's card has the file-mailbox-over-keystrokes rule, to which pair-mailbox adds the bounded read that ends each turn. What would be adopted, per the collection pack's recommendation (a proposal, not approved), in semi only: for a two-seat build and review pair, exactly one writer enforced by the coordination layer with refusals audit-logged, and a read-only critic proposing hash-sealed patches verified immediately before apply; turns that end with a bounded mailbox read, pane typing being only an accelerator; a close that needs recorded evidence plus one human ok, with secrets, deploys, migrations, deletions and history as hard stops at every level; and self-declared evidence replaced by our code-decides-done checks (tests, file, commit, live URL) before any close counts. The default, auto, reaches a finished PR with no human word, which the collection pack rules out under Haiyuan's human gate; only semi with our existing merge gate fits. Caveats: pair_evidence is trusted self-report upstream and would have to be swapped as above; how far the server enforces the single-writer rule beyond the README and protocol summary was not code-audited; the installer edits several CLIs' configs, so any trial must be scoped and reversible; split sessions need bash 4 or newer; MIT, 1 star, created 2026-10-02; README-verified only, not installed or run. Reference only; any workflow change, live-seat pilot, install, hook or settings change needs Haiyuan. No new seat. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: whystuck: names why a quiet command stalled and prints the non-interactive fix
entries.why: One-file Python idle watchdog (zero dependencies, Python 3.9+): you run any command under it, and when the output goes quiet (--idle 20 by default) it inspects the live process tree and classifies the stall as a pager, an editor, a y/N prompt, a password prompt, watch mode, a lock, a stalled TCP connect (SYN_SENT only), a server, or busy (at least 25% of a core over 0.5 s), then prints the evidence and the non-interactive fix. --json gives a machine-readable result, --kill sends SIGTERM to the process group and then SIGKILL (with a subreaper on Linux), and --explain PID diagnoses a process that is already hung. The author reports 136 tests, including a mutation-style check that removing any rule must break a case, 9 real-process snapshots and real PTY runs per rule; --demo runs 8 scenarios offline. The README states its limits plainly: DNS stalls and established-but-silent connections are not diagnosed; the server class cannot tell a healthy server from an internally hung one; macOS is best-effort (ps and lsof only, with no syscall or lock-holder detail, while Linux gets the full /proc view) and was not tested on real macOS in v0.1; Windows is unsupported (it exits 2); and --json carries the last 4,000 characters of output, with a printed secrets warning. The author's prior-art search (8 query variants, 18 Oct 2026) found no standalone agent-agnostic live-stall diagnoser; the closest were per-agent prevention lists and kill-only timeout. Why it matters here: the collection pack notes that our launch watchdog knows that a seat went quiet, not why, and that the why is usually a pager, editor or prompt a headless seat will never answer. whystuck supplies the missing diagnosis layer, the cause and a non-interactive fix at the stall, plus --explain for after-the-fact triage of a wedged pane, and the pack places it beside kept agent-chain-doctor (silent-stop checks at startup) and Cliffhanger (conversational early stops), at the process layer neither covers. We already have: every long Mac run launched in tmux with streaming output and a stale-log watchdog (~540 s) that resumes the same session (#launch), next to the EM's 15-minute heartbeat, which does not replace the watchdog (#em-loop); Mac launch skills that document symptom → action failure branches, a ~540 s stall among them, and named long-run failure modes (crash, hang, stall, api-error) whose rule is to leave a machine-readable heartbeat saying whether the run finished and what killed it (#exception-first); the rule that a stale run resumes only after the old agent process is confirmed gone, else it is parked as an unknown outcome, checked by hand because the live watchdog still kills and resumes without that check (#watchdog-resume-safety); and the rule that a new check is first run against a deliberately broken input and seen to fail (#check-can-fail), which whystuck's remove-a-rule test applies to its stall rules. What would be adopted, per the collection pack's recommendation (a proposal, not approved): the stall taxonomy as watchdog vocabulary (pager, editor, y/N prompt, password prompt, watch mode, lock, stalled connect, server, busy), each paired with its non-interactive fix, so a stale-pane alert names the cause and the remedy, not just the elapsed silence; a trial of whystuck --explain on one seat against the next genuinely wedged pane, read-only diagnosis first, with removing the binary as the rollback and --kill only after the diagnosis is trusted; and the remove-a-rule-must-break-a-test check on any stall rule we ship. Wiring it into the live watchdog would be a separate Haiyuan decision: the watchdog's no-auto-resume redesign is parked and reopens only on Haiyuan's ask (#watchdog-resume-safety), and the playbook says not to fleet-replace the watchdog without that ask (#exception-first). Caveats: the author has not tested the macOS path and our seats run on a Mac, so the trial is itself the platform test; DNS stalls and established-but-silent connections stay undiagnosed; after a --kill, a resume would still wait until the old agent process is confirmed gone (#watchdog-resume-safety); the --json output tail can carry secrets if the command prints them, and secrets stay out of vault notes and hub commits (#checklist); the test counts are the author's, read in the README, not re-run; MIT, 0 stars, created 2026-10-18; README-verified only, not installed or run. Reference only; any workflow change, live-seat install, hook or settings change needs Haiyuan. No new seat. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
